subject: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer / unit price mapping (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Tran <jamie.tran@brightcart.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer / unit price mapping (follow-up)

Hi Jamie —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can map to the AWS Marketplace private offer options: 

Recap from our discovery call:
- Primary use: customer-facing summarization + search reranker (mix of generation + embeddings).
- Expected monthly token volume (current estimate): 150M tokens/month, seasonal peak ~250M.
- Target price profile: BrightCart is evaluating target unit economics in the range of $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (total cost to BrightCart) depending on SLAs and support.
- Preferred procurement channel: AWS Marketplace Private Offer (MPO) is preferred but open to direct invoicing if MPO passthrough fees push above budget.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the token volume bucket you expect for Q3? (150M steady-state vs 250M peak)
2) Are there any internal constraints on list vs net pricing on marketplace offers?
3) I attached a quick unit-price mapping workbook — if you can share expected final budget range and which marketplace (AWS vs GCP) you want mapped, we’ll return concrete MPO price points by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-unit-price-mapping.xlsx (workbook stub), SOW-draft.pdf (stub)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer / unit price mapping (follow-up)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 
- Q3 plan: We expect to start at ~100–150M tokens/month for a controlled rollout with a target to hit ~200–250M within 6–8 weeks post-launch if things look good.
- Budget: Our procurement has signaled a target total cost of roughly $900/1M tokens (net) for committed usage; that’s the upper limit unless we get a strong SLA or dedicated capacity (which could move the needle).
- Marketplace: AWS MPO preferred. We need the MPO price broken down into list price and net after marketplace fees so our procurement team can evaluate.

Also looping Diane from Ops for usage and compliance questions.

Cheers,

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jamie Tran <jamie.tran@brightcart.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer / unit price mapping (follow-up)

Thanks Jamie — good clarity. A few notes from the partner/marketplace side (AWS):

- AWS MPO mechanics: Marketplace private offer shows a list price to the buyer but the net payout to the seller is list minus marketplace fees (and any reseller margins if applicable). There are also potential data transfer and support pass-throughs to account for.
- Typical fee impact: in our experience the MPO path can add ~10–18% on top of the net price depending on billing/reseller setup. If BrightCart needs a net of $900/1M tokens, we should model list prices in the $990–$1,100/1M range to account for MPO fees so the net stays at target.
- Alternate: direct invoice via our contract (Reserved/Dedicated) can avoid the marketplace fee but may require different procurement approvals.

I’ve pulled rough unit-price tiering based on the volumes Jamie mentioned. Attaching a short mapping doc; will also run the same numbers for GCP Marketplace and Azure if you want cross-cloud comparables.

Rafael
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
\

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Tran <jamie.tran@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart - Marketplace private offer / unit price mapping (follow-up)

Jamie / team —

Thanks — I took your Q3 volumes and Rafael’s MPO guidance and sketched three concrete pricing scenarios (all numbers are $ per 1M tokens, total cost to BrightCart):

Scenario A — MPO list mapped to net $900/1M (preferred target)
- Steady (150M/mo): list $995 -> estimated net to BrightCart $900 after ~9.6% MPO fee
- Peak (250M/mo): list $975 (volume discount) -> net ~$882 (better leverage)

Scenario B — Direct contract (no MPO fees)
- Steady: list/net $900 (no marketplace fee)
- Peak: $860 (volume discount under reserved commit)
\Scenario C — MPO conservative (higher fee pass-through)
- Steady: list $1,050 -> net ~$910 after higher marketplace fees + support pass-throughs

Notes / asks:
- Please confirm whether your procurement team needs list price explicitly on the MPO for the private offer form (some teams require list shown) or if a net-only target is sufficient.
- If you can share an expected contract term length (12 vs 24 months) we can update reserved discounts which materially change the $/1M.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will prepare a clean MPO price sheet (list vs net) for AWS and run the same table for GCP/Azure for comparison.
2) BrightCart to confirm Q3 bucket (150 vs 250M) and preferred term length.
3) Rafael to engage partner ops for MPO setup once BrightCart confirms.

I attached the quick unit-price mapping we used. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the assumptions.
—Aditya
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
